steps.note: print() shows something on the screen. Put text inside quotes.

choices.why: Correct. Quotes tell Python that Hello is text.
Without quotes, Python looks for a variable named Hello.
Parentheses do not add quotes. Python would still look for a variable named Hello.

steps.explain: The quotes mark Hello as text, and print() displays it.

steps.note: A different message goes in its own pair of quotes.

choices.why: Correct. This makes Python a text value.
This opening quote needs a matching closing quote.
Without quotes, Python treats python as a variable name.

steps.explain: The new print call displays a second piece of text.

steps.note: Python commands are case-sensitive. The built-in function is lowercase print.

choices.why: Correct. The function name is lowercase, with parentheses around its input.
Python treats Print and print as different names. Use lowercase.
In Python, the value for print goes inside parentheses.

steps.explain: Use lowercase print() with the text inside its parentheses.

steps.note: Numbers can be printed without quotes. Python keeps them as numbers.

choices.why: Correct. This is the number seven.
Quotes make this text, not a number.
Python would look for a variable named seven.

steps.explain: Without quotes, 7 is a number that print() can display.

steps.note: The opening and closing parentheses keep each print call together.

choices.why: Correct. This is a complete print call.
The opening parenthesis needs a closing parenthesis.
The brackets do not match. Close the parenthesis with ).

steps.explain: Matching parentheses show Python where the function call ends.

steps.note: Each print() call writes its value on a new line.

choices.why: Correct. This is the next text value to print.
Text needs quotes so Python does not search for a variable.
The text needs a closing quote before the parenthesis.

steps.explain: Every print call starts a fresh output line.
